subject: Access TTL for SOC 2 materials — ephemeral proxy & archival caveat
messages:
From: Oliver Trent <oliver.trent@acme-audits.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security Team <audits@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 Type II access window and bridge letter request

Hi Irene,

Hope you’re well. Our audit team is starting a supplemental evidence pull for Acme Corp and we need short-term access to Redwood’s Trust portal to review the SOC 2 Type II artifacts and related evidence. Can you provision an auditor access link for the following addresses: oliver.trent@acme-audits.com and audits@acme-corp.com?

A few specifics they asked for:
- A timeboxed download window (they typically request 72 hours to run extracts).
- A bridge letter that confirms the report period, scope of controls covered, and whether any control exceptions occurred after the period.
- Confirmation on whether full archival snapshots can be exported offline or if downloads are limited to an evidence index (we want to avoid late surprises).

Can you confirm what TTL you can provide and whether Redwood can supply a signed bridge letter? We’re trying to schedule the evidence pull for next week.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Trent
Senior Auditor — Acme Audit Services
oliver.trent@acme-audits.com
+1 (415) 555-0198
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Trent <oliver.trent@acme-audits.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II access window and bridge letter request

Hi Oliver —

Thanks for the heads up. I provisioned a one-time SSO invite for oliver.trent@acme-audits.com and audits@acme-corp.com; link below. By default our portal issues ephemeral sessions with a 48-hour TTL and download controls that limit bulk archival exports (we surface an evidence index CSV and allow per-file downloads, but do not provide a full offline archive by default).

Invite: https://trust.redwood.com/session/one-time/abc123 (expires 2026-05-16T10:03:00-07:00)

If you need a longer window (7 days), we can extend it but that requires an approval from our security team and a short justification (audit scope + reason for extended retention). We can also produce a bridge letter draft; Marissa is cc’d and will help scope the language.

Before I escalate for an extended window, can you confirm: 1) exact auditor emails (I used the two above), 2) the minimum download window required (you mentioned ~72 hours), and 3) whether Acme requires the full report PDF or additional artifacts beyond the evidence index?

I’ve attached the latest SOC 2 Type II report PDF to this message for reference (SOC2_TypeII_2025_report.pdf_stub).

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Oliver Trent <oliver.trent@acme-audits.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security Team <audits@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II access window and bridge letter request

Hi Irene — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the report.

We do need the following to avoid scheduling friction:
1) A 7-day access window (start date flexible, but the extra time is for bulk verification and re-running a couple of sampling jobs).
2) A bridge letter that explicitly states: the report covers the period Jan 1, 2025 — Dec 31, 2025; scope includes production inference runtime and platform controls; there were no known exceptions after Dec 31, 2025 through May 1, 2026 affecting the covered scopes.
3) Confirmation that the portal export policy allows auditors to download the evidence index CSV and individual artifacts, and whether there is any redaction or masking applied to logs/attachments.

We understand extended windows require sign-off; a 7-day window would materially help our ability to complete the work without repeated re-invites. Can Marissa or someone on the Redwood side confirm by EOD Monday and circulate the bridge letter draft? If possible, Acme would like a signed letter within 24 hours of confirmation.

Thanks — I’ll hold scheduling until I hear back.

Oliver
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Trent <oliver.trent@acme-audits.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II access window and bridge letter request

Oliver —

Appreciate the clarity. I looped Ben from SecOps to prepare the bridge letter language and confirm technical constraints.

What we did today:
- Reissued a one-time portal session for the two auditor addresses with a 7-day TTL (new expiry: 2026-05-21T23:59:00-07:00). Link: https://trust.redwood.com/session/one-time/def456
- Attached a draft bridge letter (bridge_letter_acme_draft.docx_stub) that follows your requested structure; Ben will review and attach a signed copy once legal signs off.
- Included the evidence index CSV for the artifacts we expose in the portal (evidence_index.csv_stub). Note: we do not provide a bulk offline archive of internal logs; downloads are per-file and some sensitive log fields are redacted per our PII policy. That redaction is limited to PII elements, not to the control evidence itself.

Next steps for you: confirm receipt of the reissued link and whether the TTL meets your schedule. Ben/Marissa — can you confirm timing for the signed bridge (Ben: security approval + Marissa: legal/CO signature) and advise if you need anything from Acme to expedite?

Thanks,
Irene
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
